notes: adapter-core: new ProviderExecutable interface matching the DelegatedAdapterBin wire shape (absent interpreter = node; entry is the python module:callable; native executes the verified store file directly) and ProviderInspection.executables as optional provider metadata validated by consumers. plugin-host: validateOperationResult's inspect case now runs validateBins after the schema + purl checks, failing closed as INVALID_RESPONSE on unsafe names, absolute/backslash/'..' paths, unknown interpreters, entry-without-python, python-without-valid-entry, >64 declarations, and duplicate names — the schema-only prose rules are enforced host-side and the safety invariants are re-asserted at the trust boundary (defense in depth; several invalid classes are already schema-rejected and stay INVALID_RESPONSE either way). The plugin's answer is preserved exactly: undefined executables stays absent, [] stays []. DelegatedCatalogProvider now sets capabilities.extensions['openpacker/artifact-bytes'] = 'host-fetch' iff the manifest admits fetch-artifact-record (same admitsOperation condition that adds 'artifact' to operations); no other extensions existed to keep. packages/plugin-host/src/manifest.ts needed no changes: layer 01 did not alter the DelegatedAdapterManifest wire type and admitsOperation semantics are unchanged. Python entry pattern reuses the opm-project bins shape /^[A-Za-z0-9_.]+:[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$/. Layer 03 acquisition can rely on the marker being present on every catalog-registered plugin today (manifest consistency requires fetch-artifact-record for the catalog capability), but the constructor guard keeps the marker honest for any future manifest shape.
deviations: None. Prettier reformatted three long lines in protocol.ts after the first commit attempt failed the pre-commit gate; formatting-only.
